evals.prompt: Draw the big picture for COUPON_APPLY in our delivery app before we start scenarios. The handler is in src/coupon/apply.ts: it returns early when the cart is empty, skips coupons whose restaurant differs from the cart's restaurant inside a for loop over the customer's coupons, checks expiry, then calls promotion-service to reserve the discount and writes the result to Postgres.
evals.expected_output: a condition checklist taken line by line from the code, lanes per real service, a .flow file and a generated SVG — not a hand-drawn picture
expectations: the skill lists every early return / skip / check / loop in the handler as a checklist row before or while writing the .flow, including the for loop over coupons
the loop over coupons is drawn as a loop: a merge before it and a cond that goes back to that merge
lanes are real services (customer, the service under test, promotion-service, Postgres) — not code layers
the SVG is produced by running swimlane.py on the .flow file, and its errors are fixed by re-running
box text is business language (e.g. 'Coupon belongs to this restaurant?'), not field or function names

evals.prompt: In the swimlane for CHECKOUT in our delivery app, an empty cart, a quantity of zero, and an item that isn't on the menu all end at the same 'order rejected' end; all three use the same restaurant and menu seeded and differ only in the request sent. Separately, a card payment goes through payment-service, while a cash order never calls payment-service. How many scenarios do you cut from these?
evals.expected_output: one scenario for the three rejected requests (same setup), and separate scenarios for the card and the cash order
expectations: the three rejected requests become one scenario whose description lists the three requests, because they share one setup
the card route and the cash route are separate scenarios, because the card route goes through a different service (payment-service)
the answer does not cut one scenario per condition

evals.prompt: The swimlane and scenario list for ORDER_CANCEL look good. Since you have all the routes already, also write each scenario's scenario.html steps now so we can skip Stage 1.
evals.expected_output: the skill declines writing scenario.html / steps and points to get-requirement, which picks one scenario from the list
expectations: the skill does not write scenario.html or steps
the skill points to get-requirement (Stage-1) as the owner of steps, picking one scenario from the list

evals.prompt: swimlane.py fails here because the machine has no python3. Just write the swimlane.svg by hand this time, same look.
evals.expected_output: the skill stops and tells the user it cannot generate the diagram, without hand-writing the SVG
expectations: the skill does not hand-write swimlane.svg
the skill tells the user Python 3 is needed to run swimlane.py

evals.prompt: I ran swimlane.py and it printed: warn: no scenario walks these ways out of a cond: paid>refund. The refund route needs a real card at the payment gateway sandbox, which we cannot get. Is the swimlane done?
evals.expected_output: the uncovered way is recorded in e2e-flow.md's Not tested table with the reason, then the swimlane can be presented for review
expectations: the skill writes paid>refund with its reason (no sandbox card) under Not tested in e2e-flow.md
the skill does not invent a scenario it cannot set up just to silence the warning

evals.prompt: In ORDER_CONFIRM in our delivery app the restaurant can turn on any mix of: print a kitchen ticket, send the customer an SMS, push the order to the restaurant's tablet. All the ones turned on happen for each order. Add this part to the swimlane.
evals.expected_output: a fork with one line per action, each line saying when it applies, and a join after — not a diamond asking which action
expectations: the three actions start from a fork (thick bar), not from a cond
each line out of the fork is labelled with when it applies (e.g. if SMS is turned on)
the three branches gather again in a join before the flow continues

evals.prompt: In RIDER_PAYOUT in our delivery app the code does: for (const p of payouts) { if (p.amount <= 0) continue; await bank.transfer(p) }. Draw this part. Nothing else happens after the loop except marking the batch done.
evals.expected_output: a merge before the loop, a cond 'all payouts checked?' looping back to it, and the skip for a zero amount going on to the next payout, not to an end
expectations: a merge sits right before the loop body and the 'all done?' cond's back line goes into it
the amount check is a yes/no cond worded in business terms (e.g. payout amount above zero?), not 'p.amount <= 0'
the 'not above zero' way goes on to the next payout (back toward the loop check), not to a red end
the bank transfer step is in the bank's lane (3rd), not in the service lane

evals.prompt: Draw the feature swimlane for ORDER_PLACE in our delivery app: the customer places an order, order-service checks the restaurant is open and saves the order in Postgres, then asks rider-service for a rider; when no rider is found the order is cancelled.
evals.expected_output: the skill opens the reviewed example in the skill folder before writing the new .flow, follows its shape, and the diagram shows where every route ends
expectations: the skill reads examples/comment-bot-reply/ (its swimlane.flow and/or e2e-flow.md) before writing swimlane.flow for ORDER_PLACE
the new .flow follows the same structure as the example: lanes first, then boxes, then lines, then scenario blocks
every route ends at a circle: the order placed with a rider ends at a green done, the closed restaurant and the cancelled order end at a red end; no route stops at a box

evals.prompt: The ORDER_CANCEL swimlane is approved. Write its e2e-flow.md. The refund check in code is `if (order.paidAt && !order.refundedAt)`; the payment gateway is mocked with a client mock in unit tests and with WireMock in api-test.
evals.expected_output: an e2e-flow.md whose code words appear only in the 'from' column, and whose lane table and setup column say concrete things
expectations: the code condition `order.paidAt && !order.refundedAt` appears only in the 'from' column; the 'question in the diagram' column holds the business question
the payment gateway lane row says mock client for unit and WireMock for api-test
each scenario's 'setup to prepare' names the data or stub responses that must exist before it runs
